title: Scientific Notation
seo_title: Grade 8 Scientific Notation Worksheets: Convert, Compare, Multiply and Divide
standard_text: Perform operations with numbers expressed in scientific notation, including problems where both decimal and scientific notation are used. Use scientific notation and choose units of appropriate size for measurements of very large or very small quantities. Interpret scientific notation that has been generated by technology.
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 scientific notation worksheets: write large and small numbers in scientific notation and standard form, compare them, find how many times greater, and multiply, divide, add and subtract. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Write a number as a × 10ⁿ, with a at least 1 and less than 10.
key_sub: Big numbers: positive n. Small numbers: negative n. Multiply → add exponents, divide → subtract.
body_html:
What is scientific notation?

Scientific notation writes a number as a × 10n, where a is at least 1 and less than 10, and n is a whole number.

Standard formScientific notationWhy
3,500,0003.5 × 106decimal point moves 6 places left
0.000424.2 × 10−4decimal point moves 4 places right

Big numbers have a positive exponent. Small numbers (less than 1) have a negative exponent.

Example

Find (6 × 108) ÷ (3 × 102).

Divide the numbers: 6 ÷ 3 = 2.

Subtract the exponents: 8 − 2 = 6.

Answer: 2 × 106

Example

How many times greater is 9 × 107 than 3 × 104?

9 ÷ 3 = 3.

107 ÷ 104 = 103.

3 × 103 = 3,000.

Answer: 3,000 times

Common mistakes

  • A first factor that is 10 or more: 35 × 105 should be 3.5 × 106.
  • The wrong sign: 0.004 is 4 × 10−3, not 4 × 103.
  • Counting places wrong: count every place the decimal point moves.
  • Adding the exponents when you divide. Subtract them.

faq.q: How do you write a number in scientific notation?
faq.a: Move the decimal point until the number is between 1 and 10. Count the places you moved. Moving left gives a positive exponent; moving right gives a negative one. 3,500,000 = 3.5 × 10⁶.

faq.q: What does a negative exponent mean in scientific notation?
faq.a: It means the number is less than 1. 4.2 × 10⁻⁴ = 0.00042.

faq.q: How do you multiply numbers in scientific notation?
faq.a: Multiply the first factors and add the exponents. Then adjust so the first factor is between 1 and 10.

items.q: Which number is written in scientific notation?
items.e: The first factor must be at least 1 and less than 10. The answer is 3.2 × 104.
Move the decimal point 8 places right: 300,000,000.
Make the first factor between 1 and 10, then change the exponent to match: 4.5 × 105.
Move the decimal point 4 places right: 17,500.

items.q: Which number is written in scientific notation?
items.e: The first factor must be between 1 and 10, and the power of 10 must be a whole number. The answer is 7 × 10−3.
Move the decimal point 6 places right: 9,010,000.
Make the first factor between 1 and 10, then change the exponent to match: 6 × 102.
Move the decimal point 3 places right: 4,400.

items.q: Which number is written in scientific notation?
items.e: 1 is allowed as the first factor; 10 is not. The answer is 1 × 106.
Move the decimal point 9 places right: 2,500,000,000.
Make the first factor between 1 and 10, then change the exponent to match: 1.23 × 10−3.
Move the decimal point 7 places right: 80,600,000.

items.q: Which number is written in scientific notation?
items.e: Only 9.99 is between 1 and 10, and it must be times a power of 10. The answer is 9.99 × 102.

Move the decimal point 5 places right: 512,300.

items.q: Which number is written in scientific notation?
items.e: 4.06 is between 1 and 10 and the exponent is a whole number. The answer is 4.06 × 10−8.

Compare the exponents first: 108 vs 107. The greater power wins: 3 × 108.

items.q: How many times greater is 6 × 108 than 2 × 105?
items.e: Divide: 6 ÷ 2 = 3, and 108 ÷ 105 = 103. So it is 3,000 times greater.
Compare the exponents first: 10−4 vs 10−5. The greater power wins: 2.5 × 10−4.

items.q: How many times greater is 9 × 107 than 3 × 104?
items.e: Divide: 9 ÷ 3 = 3, and 107 ÷ 104 = 103. So it is 3,000 times greater.
Compare the exponents first: 106 vs 109. The greater power wins: 7.1 × 109.

items.q: How many times greater is 8 × 1012 than 4 × 109?
items.e: Divide: 8 ÷ 4 = 2, and 1012 ÷ 109 = 103. So it is 2,000 times greater.
The exponents are the same, so compare 4 and 3.9: 4 × 103 is greater.

items.q: How many times greater is 5 × 106 than 1 × 103?
items.e: Divide: 5 ÷ 1 = 5, and 106 ÷ 103 = 103. So it is 5,000 times greater.
Compare the exponents first: 10−6 vs 10−3. The greater power wins: 1.2 × 10−3.

items.q: How many times greater is 1 × 109 than 2 × 106?
items.e: Divide: 1 ÷ 2 = 0.5, and 109 ÷ 106 = 103. So it is 500 times greater.
Compare the exponents first: 1012 vs 1011. The greater power wins: 8 × 1012.

items.q: How many times greater is 3 × 1010 than 1.5 × 108?
items.e: Divide: 3 ÷ 1.5 = 2, and 1010 ÷ 108 = 102. So it is 200 times greater.
The exponents are the same, so compare 5.5 and 5.4: 5.5 × 10−2 is greater.

items.q: How many times greater is 4 × 10−3 than 2 × 10−6?
items.e: Divide: 4 ÷ 2 = 2, and 10−3 ÷ 10−6 = 103. So it is 2,000 times greater.
Compare the exponents first: 1010 vs 1011. The greater power wins: 2 × 1011.

items.q: How many times greater is 7 × 105 than 7 × 102?
items.e: Divide: 7 ÷ 7 = 1, and 105 ÷ 102 = 103. So it is 1,000 times greater.

items.q: How many times greater is 1.2 × 107 than 4 × 104?
items.e: Divide: 1.2 ÷ 4 = 0.3, and 107 ÷ 104 = 103. So it is 300 times greater.

items.q: How many times greater is 2 × 109 than 5 × 106?
items.e: Divide: 2 ÷ 5 = 0.4, and 109 ÷ 106 = 103. So it is 400 times greater.

items.q: How many times greater is 6 × 10−2 than 3 × 10−5?
items.e: Divide: 6 ÷ 3 = 2, and 10−2 ÷ 10−5 = 103. So it is 2,000 times greater.

items.q: How many times greater is 9 × 1011 than 3 × 107?
items.e: Divide: 9 ÷ 3 = 3, and 1011 ÷ 107 = 104. So it is 30,000 times greater.

items.q: Find (2 × 103) × (3 × 104). Write the answer in scientific notation.
items.e: Multiply the numbers: 2 × 3 = 6. Add the exponents: 107. The answer is 6 × 107.

items.q: The Sun is about 1.5 × 10<sup>8</sup> km from Earth. The Moon is about 3.8 × 10<sup>5</sup> km away. About how many times farther is the Sun?
Find (4 × 105) × (2 × 10−2). Write the answer in scientific notation.
items.e: Multiply the numbers: 4 × 2 = 8. Add the exponents: 103. The answer is 8 × 103.

items.q: A calculator shows 4.2E−5. What number is it?
Find (6 × 108) ÷ (3 × 102). Write the answer in scientific notation.
items.e: Divide the numbers: 6 ÷ 3 = 2. Subtract the exponents: 106. The answer is 2 × 106.

items.q: Find (5 × 107) × (4 × 103). Write the answer in scientific notation.
items.e: Multiply the numbers: 5 × 4 = 20. Add the exponents: 1010. Adjust so the first factor is between 1 and 10. The answer is 2 × 1011.

items.q: A calculator shows 7.3E9. What number is it?
Find (9 × 106) ÷ (3 × 108). Write the answer in scientific notation.
items.e: Divide the numbers: 9 ÷ 3 = 3. Subtract the exponents: 10−2. The answer is 3 × 10−2.

items.q: A virus is about 1 × 10<sup>−7</sup> m long. A bacterium is about 2 × 10<sup>−6</sup> m long. How many times longer is the bacterium?
Find (1.5 × 104) × (6 × 105). Write the answer in scientific notation.
items.e: Multiply the numbers: 1.5 × 6 = 9. Add the exponents: 109. The answer is 9 × 109.

items.q: Find (8 × 10−3) ÷ (2 × 10−7). Write the answer in scientific notation.
items.e: Divide the numbers: 8 ÷ 2 = 4. Subtract the exponents: 104. The answer is 4 × 104.

items.q: A hard drive holds 2 × 10<sup>12</sup> bytes. A photo is 4 × 10<sup>6</sup> bytes. How many photos fit?
Find (2.5 × 106) × (4 × 10−9). Write the answer in scientific notation.
items.e: Multiply the numbers: 2.5 × 4 = 10. Add the exponents: 10−3. Adjust so the first factor is between 1 and 10. The answer is 1 × 10−2.

items.q: Light travels about 3 × 10<sup>5</sup> km each second. How far does it travel in 6 × 10<sup>1</sup> seconds (1 minute)?
Find (7.2 × 1010) ÷ (2.4 × 104). Write the answer in scientific notation.
items.e: Divide the numbers: 7.2 ÷ 2.4 = 3. Subtract the exponents: 106. The answer is 3 × 106.

items.q: The US population is about 3.3 × 10<sup>8</sup>. Each person drinks about 2 × 10<sup>2</sup> liters of milk a year. About how much is that in all?
Find (3 × 109) × (3 × 109). Write the answer in scientific notation.
items.e: Multiply the numbers: 3 × 3 = 9. Add the exponents: 1018. The answer is 9 × 1018.

items.q: Earth’s mass is about 6 × 10<sup>24</sup> kg. Jupiter’s is about 1.9 × 10<sup>27</sup> kg. About how many times heavier is Jupiter?
